transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello. Well... I suppose it's about bridges. 

If I'm in the car and... and a bridge crossing becomes unavoidable... I just... my heart starts pounding. My hands get all damp on the steering wheel, or the armrest if I'm just sitting there. It's... well, it's a terrible rush of fear. Even before I'm actually on the bridge. 

So... that's what brings me in.
Is your fear specifically related to certain types of bridges, like high ones, ones over water, or ones that look unstable, or does it happen with all bridges?

Well... mostly the high ones, I suppose. 

I mean, I know perfectly well that thousands of cars cross those bridges every day. But... when I see a high span on a map, or... or just ahead through the windshield... it just feels to me as if the whole thing is waiting to drop away under us. 

So... yes. The high ones.
Do you find yourself going out of your way to avoid driving over high bridges, even if it means taking a longer route?

Well... yes. I do. 

It's been... more than two years now, I suppose. I plan all my errands around it. I... I used to go to San Juan, or into Seattle for the theater, but... I gave that up. 

If I really have no choice, I... well, I have to study the route beforehand. And the timing has to be just right. Even then, I can't do it alone. I need someone else in the car with me, and I just... I sit there, terrified, the whole way across. So... yes, I avoid them.
Have you ever experienced this same kind of intense fear in other situations, like being in crowds, open spaces, or using public transportation?

Well... no. I don't think so. 

I haven't noticed anything like that with crowds or buses. It's... just the bridges, really.
Do you ever experience symptoms like a pounding heart, sweating, or trembling in situations other than when you're near a high bridge?

Well... no. Not that I've noticed. 

It's really just... just the bridges. I don't get worked up like that otherwise.
